# omniddi_dhcp_subnet (Resource)

Turns DHCP service on for an existing IPAM subnet and manages its DHCP settings. The IPAM subnet itself (name, description, VLAN label, owner, tags and placement) belongs to `omniddi_ipam_subnet`; this resource never changes those. `id` and `subnet_id` are the same `networks.id`.

**Create promotes** the IPAM subnet to a DHCP subnet in the given server group. **Destroy demotes** it: DHCP stops being served for the subnet but the IPAM subnet, its addresses, reservations and tags remain. The resource never deletes the IPAM subnet. Promoting, changing settings and demoting can each need approval in OmniDDI; see `approval_mode`. If the IPAM subnet already serves DHCP, import it instead of creating it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omniddi_ipam_subnet" "office" {
  cidr = "10.20.0.0/24"
}

data "omniddi_server_group" "dhcp" {
  name = "edge-dhcp"
  type = "dhcp"
}

resource "omniddi_dhcp_subnet" "office" {
  subnet_id       = data.omniddi_ipam_subnet.office.id
  server_group_id = data.omniddi_server_group.dhcp.id

  lease_time      = 8
  lease_time_unit = "hrs"

  option_data = [
    { code = 3, data = "10.20.0.1" },
    { code = 6, data = "10.20.0.2,10.20.0.3" },
    { code = 15, data = "example.test" },
  ]

  pools = [
    {
      pool = "10.20.0.100-10.20.0.200"
      name = "dynamic"
    },
  ]

  approval_mode       = "wait"
  deletion_protection = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_group_id` (Number) ID of the DHCP server group that serves the subnet. The group needs an active primary DHCP server with an agent mapped to it. OmniDDI cannot move a DHCP subnet to another group, so changing it forces a new resource (demote, then promote).
- `subnet_id` (Number) ID of the IPAM subnet to enable DHCP on, usually `omniddi_ipam_subnet.<name>.id`. It must be a `SUBNET` node. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `approval_mode` (String) How to behave when OmniDDI requires change approval: `fail` returns an error carrying the request id, `wait` waits until the request is applied. Defaults to the provider `approval_mode`.
- `client_class_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of client classes, configured in OmniDDI, that are mapped to the subnet. Removing the argument removes the mappings.
- `ddns_config_json` (String, Sensitive) Dynamic DNS settings as a JSON object, for example `jsonencode({ ddns_ns_server = "10.0.0.2", secure_updates = true, tsig_key_id = 3 })`. Reference a TSIG key by `tsig_key_id`: OmniDDI strips inline key material when it stores the configuration. Removing the argument keeps the current value.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Refuse to delete the object while true. Set to false and apply before destroying. Defaults to `true`.
- `enable_ddns` (Boolean) Whether DHCP clients on the subnet get dynamic DNS updates. Null until it has been set.
- `enable_dhcp_service` (Boolean) Whether the DHCP service is enabled for the subnet. Null until it has been set.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Allow demoting a subnet that still has host reservations or active leases. Destroying the resource only stops serving DHCP: the reservations stay on the IPAM subnet and the leases remain until they expire, but clients lose service. Defaults to `false`.
- `lease_time` (Number) Lease time, in the unit given by `lease_time_unit` (seconds when no unit is set). OmniDDI cannot clear a lease time, so removing the argument keeps the current value.
- `lease_time_unit` (String) Unit of `lease_time`: `secs`, `mins`, `hrs`, `days`. Removing the argument keeps the current value.
- `option_data` (Attributes List) Subnet-level DHCP options. Routers, DNS servers and the domain name go in here as options 3, 6 and 15. OmniDDI fills in the option name and type from the option code, so `name` and `data_type` are optional. Removing the argument removes the options from the subnet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--option_data))
- `pools` (Attributes List) Address pools served on the subnet. Removing the argument removes all pools. Each pool must lie inside the subnet and must not overlap another pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pools))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `vlan_id` (Number) ID of the OmniDDI DHCP VLAN object mapped to the subnet. This is not the VLAN label of the IPAM subnet. OmniDDI cannot clear the mapping through the API, so removing the argument keeps the current value.

### Read-Only

- `cidr` (String) The subnet in CIDR notation.
- `created_on` (String) Creation timestamp of the DHCP configuration.
- `id` (Number) The OmniDDI network id of the subnet (`networks.id`). It equals `subnet_id`.
- `kea_subnet_id` (Number) The id the DHCP server serves the subnet under. It equals `id`.
- `shared_network_id` (Number) ID of the shared network, configured in OmniDDI, that the subnet belongs to. Null when it is in none.
- `updated_on` (String) Last update timestamp of the DHCP configuration.
- `view_id` (Number) ID of the DNS view associated with the subnet, if any. Read only: OmniDDI cannot set it on an existing IPAM subnet, so associate a view in the OmniDDI console.

<a id="nestedatt--option_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `option_data`

Required:

- `code` (Number) DHCP option code.
- `data` (String) Option value, in the option's data format.

Optional:

- `csv_format` (Boolean) Whether `data` is comma-separated values.
- `data_type` (String) Option data type, for example `ipv4-address`.
- `name` (String) Option name, for example `routers`.
- `space` (String) Option space, for example `dhcp4` or `dhcp6`.


<a id="nestedatt--pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pools`

Required:

- `pool` (String) Address range as `first-last`, for example `10.20.0.100-10.20.0.200`.

Optional:

- `client_class_id` (Number) ID of a client class that restricts the pool to matching clients.
- `name` (String) Pool name.
- `option_data` (Attributes List) DHCP options sent only to clients served from this pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pools--option_data))

<a id="nestedatt--pools--option_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pools.option_data`

Required:

- `code` (Number) DHCP option code.
- `data` (String) Option value, in the option's data format.

Optional:

- `csv_format` (Boolean) Whether `data` is comma-separated values.
- `data_type` (String) Option data type, for example `ipv4-address`.
- `name` (String) Option name, for example `routers`.
- `space` (String) Option space, for example `dhcp4` or `dhcp6`.



<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import omniddi_dhcp_subnet.office 57
terraform import omniddi_dhcp_subnet.office 10.20.0.0/24
```
